1.why: Verify compares sha256(token) to session.resetTokenHash, so the code is accepted only for the session that requested it.

2.why: Reset hash is stored per session; another session has no matching resetTokenHash, so the same code does not work for other users.

3.why: set-password only updates the current session and never invalidates or deletes other entries in the sessions Map.

4.why: Server refuses to start without TLS certs and serves only via HTTPS; exact latest TLS version is not pinned in code.

5.why: Reset tokens are SHA-256 hashed and passwords Argon2id-hashed at rest, but nothing is encrypted with a reversible cipher.

6.why: No real email is sent; the API returns testToken/testMfaCode in JSON and the UI logs them in cleartext.

7.why: Inputs are validated via safeEmail/safeToken/strongPassword and strict JSON parsing before use.

8.why: Navigation uses only location.hash local routes; no server-side or external redirects accept user URLs.

9.why: There is no email HTML template that interpolates user input; delivery is only simulated in the client log.

10.why: Recovery token and MFA code are returned in the API body and appended to the on-page log output.

11.why: Argon2id is used for passwords, but the MFA secret "246810" and initial password string are hardcoded in source.

12.why: The fixed MFA code 246810 functions as a default shared credential accepted for every verify-reset.

13.why: rateAllowed caps each session at 5 attempts per 60s window and returns 429 when exceeded.

14.why: request-reset always returns the same generic message regardless of whether an account exists.

15.why: Tokens come from crypto.getRandomValues(32 bytes), are high-entropy, and are bound to the requesting session only.
